| Layout system | Every route | Three App Router route-group layouts: `AppShell` (freelancer sidebar/top bar, support-session banner), `PortalShell` (branded header with logo, `--brand` vars, referral mark, help link; mobile-first single column), `OpsShell` (operator console). Nested project layout supplies project tabs. Layouts perform the realm guard (`requireFreelancer`, `requirePortalContact`, `requireOperator`) | `src/app/(freelancer)/app/layout.tsx`, `src/app/(portal)/portal/[handle]/layout.tsx`, `src/app/(ops)/ops/layout.tsx`; shells in `src/shared/components/` | Next.js layouts, Tailwind tokens, `src/shared/lib/authz` |
| Navigation | All shells | Config-driven nav arrays per shell; active state from `usePathname()` prefix match with `aria-current="page"`; desktop sidebar, mobile bottom-sheet (Radix Dialog) under 768 px; portal uses a header with back-links rather than a sidebar | `src/shared/components/nav/` | shadcn/ui Sheet/NavigationMenu, Next.js `Link` |
| Error handling | Every route and action | Route-level `error.tsx` boundaries render a recoverable message with Retry that preserves typed input (forms keep state via `useActionState`); `not-found.tsx` for out-of-scope records returns the same "not available" explanation as a missing record so isolation never leaks existence (Access Matrix note); server actions return typed failures instead of throwing for expected cases; unexpected errors reported to Sentry with PII scrubbing (tooling decision ADR-031) | `src/app/**/error.tsx`, `src/shared/lib/telemetry/sentry.ts`, `src/shared/components/ErrorState.tsx` | Sentry SDK, `defineAction` result types |
| Loading / empty states | Every data-backed screen | `loading.tsx` per route segment renders skeletons matching the final layout (ASMP-27 "real progress while loading"); upload and export flows show determinate progress; `EmptyState` component with one primary next action; `OfflineBanner` driven by `useOnline()` states plainly which actions need a connection | `src/app/**/loading.tsx`, `src/shared/components/Skeletons.tsx`, `EmptyState.tsx`, `OfflineBanner.tsx` | React Suspense streaming, shadcn/ui Skeleton |
| Form handling | All mutation forms (≤7 inputs per profile Complex forms = No) | Server actions + React 19 `useActionState`; validation rules are plain TypeScript functions in each feature's `rules/` run on the client for instant feedback and again on the server as authority; hidden `version` field for reject-with-refresh; submit button disabled while pending to prevent double submission; on `conflict` the form shows the current values and keeps the user's input for re-apply | `src/features/*/components/*Form.tsx`, `src/features/*/rules/`, `src/shared/lib/authz/define-action.ts` | Next.js server actions, shadcn/ui Form primitives (Radix Label), ADR-014 version tokens |
| Toast / notification | Feedback after non-navigating actions and background outcomes | Radix Toast via shadcn/ui, bottom-center on mobile and bottom-right on desktop, `aria-live="polite"` (assertive for failures), auto-dismiss after 5 s except errors which persist until dismissed; never used as the only record of a failure that needs action (those render inline) | `src/shared/components/ui/toast.tsx`, `src/shared/hooks/useToast.ts` | Radix Toast |
| Authorization & support-session guard | Every server action, route handler, query and job touching account data | `defineAction()` / `defineQuery()` wrappers resolve the realm session, enforce role (Access Matrix), inject the account and client scope into data-access calls, and reject all mutations while an operator support session is active; operator reads use a read-only Postgres role connection as a second layer (feasibility FEAT-31 mitigation); a test enumerates every exported action and asserts rejection under a support session | `src/shared/lib/authz/` | Better Auth sessions, portal sessions, Drizzle read-only client |
| Versioned & offline mutations | Contended records and the Offline-signal specs | `useVersionedMutation` hook wraps TanStack Query mutations with the version token and conflict handling; only allow-listed mutation keys (`comment.create`, `schedule.save`) persist while offline, replayed in order and re-authorized on the server; persisted cache is cleared on sign-out | `src/shared/hooks/useVersionedMutation.ts`, `src/shared/lib/query-client.ts` | TanStack Query v5, IndexedDB persister |
| Money & date formatting | Every amount and timestamp shown or emailed | `formatMoney(amountMinor, currency)` and `formatDateTime(instant, tz)` wrappers over Intl; freelancer time zone for schedule semantics, viewer time zone for display (FEAT-15.SPEC-006); per-currency grouping, never summed across currencies (XBR-18) | `src/shared/lib/money.ts`, `src/shared/lib/datetime.ts` | Native Intl APIs |

## 11. Authentication & Access Architecture

### Authentication & Identity

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Context | Authentication = Yes, role-based (profile Section 3): FEAT-05.SPEC-001–007 magic-link portal access for client contacts, FEAT-20.SPEC-001 sign-up, FEAT-21.SPEC-003/005/006 login & security, email change with 24 h re-verification, sign-out other sessions; 4 roles in the Access Matrix (Freelancer, Client Primary Contact, Client Reviewer Contact, Support Operator); "a person who is a contact for several freelancers holds a separate Client Contact per freelancer" (profile Section 5); strict isolation and read-only operator (ASMP-23); contact erasure "ends access immediately" (XBR-27); feasibility FEAT-05: managed providers need the contact-per-freelancer identity mapped onto their user model and hold GDPR-class emails in a vendor store, while Better Auth or a thin token table keeps the mapping in the app's schema; magic-link prefetch risk to the ≥95% first-try target |
| Recommended | Better Auth (open-source library, sessions and accounts in Neon via Drizzle) for the freelancer and operator realm — email magic link plus email/password sign-in, email verification, multi-session listing and revocation, admin plugin for the operator role; plus an application-owned client-portal realm: hashed single-use magic-link tokens scoped to one Client Contact record (24 h expiry per `magic-link-expiry-window`, earlier unused tokens invalidated on re-request), consumed only by an explicit confirm POST on the verification landing, issuing a database-backed portal session |
| Rationale | Better Auth keeps identity data in the application database (landscape: "low lock-in (data in own DB)"; infrastructure cost only), which removes a GDPR sub-processor and lets contact erasure, session revocation and account deletion happen in the same transaction as the record change (FEAT-18.SPEC-009, FEAT-24.SPEC-004). Client contacts are per-freelancer records, not global users; modelling them as a separate, deliberately small realm keyed by Client Contact id fits that shape exactly, where a managed provider would force one-user-many-identities mapping (feasibility FEAT-05). The confirm-click interstitial mitigates scanner prefetch consumption (feasibility risk table). Clerk's free tier would be affordable, but it adds vendor-held contact data and does not model per-freelancer identities natively. |

**Alternatives:**

| Alternative | Cost Profile | Operational Complexity | Scale Ceiling | Lock-in | Team Skill Demand | Choose instead when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Clerk | Free to 50K monthly retained users; then $25/month plus per-MRU overage | Low — hosted UI, SDKs, multi-session built in | High | Medium–High — users in vendor store, export possible | Mainstream | The team wants hosted sign-in UI, MFA and bot protection for freelancers out of the box and accepts a vendor holding freelancer emails; the portal realm stays application-owned either way |
| Supabase Auth | Free 50,000 MAU; Pro $25/month incl. 100,000 MAU | Low with Supabase Postgres | High | Medium — GoTrue open source exit | Supabase + RLS | The Database decision switches to Supabase and row-level security becomes the primary client-isolation enforcement point |
| WorkOS AuthKit | Free to 1M MAU; SSO from $125/month per connection | Low — SDKs | Very high | Medium–High — hosted user store | Mainstream | Agency or enterprise freelancers require SAML SSO for their own staff (not in any spec today) |

### Session Model

Two session realms, both **database-backed opaque sessions** in Neon, delivered as `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax` cookies with only a random session identifier in the cookie (hash stored server-side), so revocation is immediate by row deletion:

- **Freelancer / operator (Better Auth):** cookie `cr_session` on the app host; Assumption — 30-day rolling lifetime refreshed on activity at most once per day, 12-hour absolute lifetime for operator accounts; sessions listed on Login & Security and revocable individually or all-but-current (FEAT-21.SPEC-006); email change keeps the old address active until the new one is verified within 24 hours (FEAT-21.SPEC-005).
- **Client portal (application-owned):** cookie `cr_portal` scoped to the serving host (shared address or the freelancer's verified custom domain — sessions are per host, per feasibility Open Question 12); one session binds exactly one Client Contact id and therefore one client company of one freelancer; Assumption — 30-day rolling lifetime; role (Primary/Reviewer) is read from the Client Contact row on every request rather than cached in the session, so role changes and removals take effect on the next request (FEAT-18.SPEC-008, XBR-27).
- **Operator support session (FEAT-31):** a `support_access_session` row opened by the operator against one freelancer account; while open, the operator's requests carry the target account scope with read-only enforcement; `last_activity_at` is updated per request and a Trigger.dev task closes sessions after 15 minutes of inactivity (`support-session-inactivity-timeout-minutes`).

Magic-link and portal tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes; sign-in email requests are rate-limited per email and IP in Postgres (Assumption — 5 per hour per address).

### User Model Fields

Freelancer/operator identity (`user` table, shared with Better Auth): `id`, `email` (unique, sign-in email), `email_verified_at`, `pending_email`, `pending_email_expires_at`, `display_name`, `role` (`freelancer` | `operator`), `time_zone` (IANA), `onboarding_state`, `created_at`, `deletion_state` (`active` | `hold` | `committed`), `deleted_at`; plus Better Auth `account` (credential/provider rows) and `session` (`id`, `user_id`, `token_hash`, `expires_at`, `created_at`, `last_seen_at`, `user_agent`) tables. The freelancer's business profile lives on the Freelancer Account entity (one-to-one with `user` where `role = freelancer`).

Client-portal identity (on the Client Contact entity, per freelancer): `id`, `freelancer_account_id`, `client_id`, `email` (unique per client), `name`, `portal_role` (`primary` | `reviewer`), `status` (`invited` | `active` | `removed`), `invited_by_contact_id`, `last_sign_in_at`, `erased_at`, `help_dismissals`; `portal_token` (`id`, `client_contact_id`, `token_hash`, `expires_at`, `consumed_at`, `created_at`); `portal_session` (`id`, `client_contact_id`, `host`, `token_hash`, `created_at`, `expires_at`, `last_seen_at`). Support: `support_access_session` (`id`, `operator_user_id`, `freelancer_account_id`, `opened_at`, `last_activity_at`, `closed_at`, `close_reason`). The Schema Designer owns final column types and constraints.

| Route / Route Group | Access Requirement | Unauthenticated Experience |
|--------------------|--------------------|----------------------------|
| `/`, `/signup`, `/sign-in`, `/r/[referralToken]` | Public | -- |
| `/app/**` (freelancer workspace; FEAT-01, 02, 04, 06, 08.SPEC-002, 09–13, 15–25, 27–29, 30.SPEC-002, 31.SPEC-001, 32) | Authenticated, role-gated (freelancer) — or operator with an open support session for that account (read-only) | Redirect to `/sign-in?next=…` |
| `/portal/[handle]/sign-in`, `/portal/[handle]/verify` (FEAT-05.SPEC-001, FEAT-05.SPEC-002) | Public within the portal | -- (expired/used link shows recovery with a request-new-link action, FEAT-05.SPEC-002) |
| `/portal/[handle]/**` other routes (FEAT-03, 04.SPEC-002, 05.SPEC-003, 07, 08.SPEC-001, 09.SPEC-002, 10.SPEC-001, 17.SPEC-002, 18.SPEC-004, 26, 30.SPEC-003) | Authenticated portal contact of a client of that freelancer; records filtered to the contact's own client (FEAT-05.SPEC-007) | Redirect to `/portal/[handle]/sign-in` with the target preserved; out-of-scope records show the plain "not available — request a fresh link" explanation, never another company's data |
| `/portal/[handle]/projects/[projectId]/proposal/**` accept, request changes, sign (FEAT-03.SPEC-001, FEAT-03.SPEC-002, FEAT-26.SPEC-001) | Role-gated (Primary) — Reviewers cannot see proposals (FEAT-03.SPEC-005) | Reviewer sees "not available" |
| `/portal/[handle]/milestones/[milestoneId]` approve action (FEAT-08.SPEC-001) | Role-gated (Primary) for approve; Reviewer view and comment only (FEAT-08.SPEC-006) | Approve control hidden for Reviewers |
| `/portal/[handle]/invoices/**` (FEAT-09.SPEC-002, FEAT-10.SPEC-001) | Role-gated (Primary) (FEAT-09.SPEC-006) | Reviewer sees "not available" |
| `/portal/[handle]/team/invite` (FEAT-18.SPEC-004) | Role-gated (Primary) | Reviewer sees "not available" |
| `/ops/**` (FEAT-31.SPEC-002) | Role-gated (operator) | 404 for non-operators; redirect to `/sign-in` when signed out |
| `/api/webhooks/*` | Provider signature verification (no session) | 401 on invalid signature |
| `/api/uploads/*`, `/api/files/*` | Authenticated freelancer (uploads); authorized viewer of the version (files); operator always refused for file downloads (XBR-29) | 401/403 JSON |

|----------------------|---------------------------|---------------------------|-------------------|

## 12. Development Conventions

### Naming Conventions

| Category | Convention | Example |
|----------|-----------|---------|
| Files (components) | PascalCase `.tsx`, one exported component per file | `MilestoneApprovalView.tsx` |
| Files (utilities) | kebab-case `.ts`; actions named verb-noun | `record-acceptance.ts`, `money.ts` |
| Components | PascalCase, suffix by role (`View`, `Form`, `List`, `Dialog`) | `export function InvoiceList()` |
| Functions | camelCase verb-first; server actions end without suffix; queries start with `get`/`list` | `acceptProposal()`, `listInvoicesForAccount()` |
| CSS classes | Tailwind utilities in markup; token names kebab-case CSS variables; no custom class names except `cr-print-*` print helpers | `className="bg-[--brand] text-[--brand-foreground]"` |
| Database tables | snake_case, singular, entity-named; columns snake_case; money columns suffixed `_minor` | `invoice`, `client_contact`, `amount_minor` |
| Routes | kebab-case path segments, plural resource nouns, `[camelCaseId]` params | `/app/invoices/[invoiceId]/record-payment` |

### Component Structure

Order within a component file: (1) `'use client'` directive only when interactivity requires it — Server Components are the default; (2) imports per the ordering below; (3) exported `Props` type; (4) the component function; (5) small private sub-components; (6) no default exports except Next.js route files (`page.tsx`, `layout.tsx`). Data access never happens inside client components — they receive data from a Server Component parent or TanStack Query hooks that call server actions.

```tsx
import { formatMoney } from '@shared/lib/money';
import type { InvoiceSummary } from '../queries/list-invoices';

export type InvoiceRowProps = { invoice: InvoiceSummary };

export function InvoiceRow({ invoice }: InvoiceRowProps) {
  return <li>{invoice.number} · {formatMoney(invoice.amountMinor, invoice.currency)}</li>;
}
```

### Import Ordering

Groups separated by a blank line, enforced by ESLint `import/order`: (1) React/Next.js, (2) third-party packages, (3) `@shared/*` and `@db/*` aliases, (4) `@features/*` (other features only through their public `index.ts`), (5) relative imports, (6) type-only imports last.

```ts
import { notFound } from 'next/navigation';

import { and, eq } from 'drizzle-orm';

import { db } from '@shared/lib/db';
import { defineAction } from '@shared/lib/authz';

import { generateInvoice } from '@features/feat-09-invoice-generation-sending';

import { assertAcceptable } from '../rules/acceptance-rules';

import type { ActionResult } from '@shared/lib/authz';
```

### TypeScript Usage

`strict: true` plus `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` — financial correctness (ASMP-25) and 60 Logic/Rule specs justify the strictest settings (ADR-028). Prefer `type` aliases for data shapes and discriminated unions (`ActionResult`); use `interface` only for extensible object contracts such as integration client interfaces. `any` is banned (`@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: error`); use `unknown` with narrowing at boundaries (webhook payloads are parsed and narrowed before use). Money is a branded type `MinorUnits` so raw numbers cannot be passed as amounts. Database row types are inferred from the Drizzle schema (`typeof invoice.$inferSelect`), never hand-written.

### Path Aliases

Defined in `tsconfig.json` `compilerOptions.paths`:

```json
{
  "@/*": ["./src/*"],
  "@features/*": ["./src/features/*"],
  "@shared/*": ["./src/shared/*"],
  "@db/*": ["./src/db/*"],
  "@jobs/*": ["./src/jobs/*"]
}
```

## 13. Deployment & Environments

### Hosting & Environments

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Context | ADR-001 Next.js 16 with ADR-002 framework server layer; ADR-012 moves long-running work off the web host; ASMP-26 no uptime target; worldwide clients mostly on mobile (BRIEF.md Geography/Devices) with the ~2 s target (ASMP-21); budget ~$100/month; custom domains via the host (ADR-018); preview environments wanted for a 33-feature codebase |
| Recommended | Vercel Pro ($20/seat/month incl. $20 usage credit and 1 TB transfer) — production and per-branch preview deployments, Node.js runtime functions in one region co-located with the Neon project (Assumption — an EU region by default, Section 2), global CDN for static assets |
| Rationale | The landscape rates Vercel "native Next.js hosting, preview environments per branch, CDN" with Low integration effort; Hobby is non-commercial only, so Pro is the floor. With scheduled and long-running work on Trigger.dev, the host only serves request/response traffic, where serverless scale-to-zero fits human-paced load. Preview deployments paired with Neon branches give every pull request an isolated, realistic environment. Platform coupling is contained: the app is a standard Next.js build that also runs on container hosts (alternatives below). |

**Alternatives:**

| Render | Fixed instance prices plus workspace fee; sample stack ~$30/month | Low — web service, cron, workers, managed Postgres in one place | High | Low — standard containers | Mainstream | The team prefers always-on containers with an in-house worker (enabling pg-boss instead of Trigger.dev) and predictable fixed pricing |
| Fly.io | Per-second machine billing; sample Node+Postgres stack ~$12/month | Medium — CLI-first, Dockerfile | High; regions near users | Low — standard containers | Docker/Fly CLI | Multi-region serving close to worldwide clients becomes necessary to hit ASMP-21 after measurement, or cost pressure demands the cheapest compute |
| Railway | Hobby $5/month, Pro $20/month plus usage; sample stack ~$37/month | Low — Git deploys, one-click Postgres and workers | Medium–High | Low | Mainstream | A small team wants container hosting with minimal ops and co-located workers, without Vercel-specific features |

### CI/CD & Delivery

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Context | 33 features, 220 specs with financial-correctness rules (ASMP-25) requiring automated checks before promotion (landscape CI/CD area); migration-based schema changes (Section 6); Trigger.dev tasks deployed alongside the web app; Vercel hosting (ADR-029) |
| Recommended | GitHub Actions for checks (typecheck, lint, unit tests for Logic/Rule functions, integration tests against a Neon branch incl. the support-session mutation sweep, Playwright e2e against the preview URL) and for migrations and Trigger.dev deploys; Vercel Git integration for build-and-deploy with a preview per pull request; production promotion from `main` gated on a protected GitHub environment |
| Rationale | GitHub Actions is "native to GitHub repos; environments with approval gates" with 2,000 free minutes/month (Free) or 3,000 (Team) — enough for this codebase at launch; platform-native Vercel deploys give previews without writing deploy scripts, while Actions supplies the test runner that platform pipelines lack (landscape note "tests still need a separate runner"). Migrations run in Actions before promotion so schema and code ship together. |

**Alternatives:**

| Alternative | Cost Profile | Operational Complexity | Scale Ceiling | Lock-in | Team Skill Demand | Choose instead when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GitLab CI/CD | Free 400 min/month; Premium from $29/user/month | Medium — requires GitLab code hosting | High | Medium — GitLab syntax | GitLab | The team's code already lives on GitLab |
| CircleCI | Free 6,000 credits/month; Performance $15 per 25,000 credits | Low–Medium | High | Medium — CircleCI config | CircleCI | Test suites grow long enough that parallel test splitting beyond Actions' runners becomes the bottleneck |
| Platform-native deploy pipelines only (Vercel Git deploys) | Included with hosting | Low | Medium | Medium — tied to host | Minimal | Never on its own for this product — only acceptable during an initial prototype before financial rules are implemented, since it runs no tests |

**Environment topology:**

- **Local development** — developer machine; Docker Postgres or a personal Neon branch; Stripe, Resend and Documenso test keys; dev R2 bucket or MinIO; `trigger dev` for jobs. Secrets in `.env.local` (never committed).
- **Preview** — one Vercel preview deployment per pull request, paired with an ephemeral Neon branch created from staging data-free schema and seeded by `src/db/seed.ts`; test-mode keys for Stripe, Resend (test key), Documenso; dev R2 bucket; Trigger.dev `preview` environment. Used for review and e2e tests.
- **Staging** — deploys from `main` automatically; its own Neon branch with migrated schema and synthetic data, Stripe test mode with test connected accounts, a staging sending subdomain, a staging R2 bucket; Trigger.dev `staging` environment. Used to verify migrations and webhook flows end to end.
- **Production** — promoted from a green `main` commit via the protected `production` GitHub environment (manual approval); production Neon branch with point-in-time restore; live Stripe keys; production R2 buckets and sending domains; Trigger.dev `prod` environment. Secrets live in Vercel and Trigger.dev environment variables per environment and in GitHub environment secrets for CI; no secret is shared between environments.

**Infrastructure as code:** Not warranted at launch — the stack is five managed services configured through their dashboards and a handful of environment variables, operated by a small team (Section 2 load is modest). The trigger that changes the answer: a second region, a second production project (e.g. EU/US split for data residency), or more than ~10 environment-specific secrets per service — at that point adopt Terraform (Vercel, Cloudflare and Neon providers) for reproducible environments.

### Observability & Operations

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Context | ASMP-26: no uptime target, but "emails that fail to deliver are surfaced to the freelancer within minutes rather than lost"; Background processing = Yes with minute-level sweeps whose silent failure breaks FEAT-11 "exactly 3 days" reminders (feasibility FEAT-11 risk); Compliance/privacy = Yes (GDPR-class data must not leak into logs); FEAT-13 audit trail is evidentiary and separate from operational logs (feasibility FEAT-13); budget ~$100/month |
| Recommended | Sentry Team ($26/month incl. 50K errors) for error tracking and tracing across Next.js and Trigger.dev, Sentry Cron Monitors on every scheduled task (outbox sweep, reminder sweep, retention purge, support auto-close) and an uptime check on the portal and webhook endpoints; Grafana Cloud free tier (Loki) as the Vercel log-drain and Trigger.dev log destination with alert rules on webhook-processing failures and outbox backlog age; PII scrubbing (emails, names, document content) at the SDK and log-formatter level |
| Rationale | Sentry covers errors, performance and missed-schedule detection in one SDK per framework (landscape: "Low — SDK per framework") at a fixed cost inside the budget; cron monitors directly address the missed-sweep risk behind FEAT-11 and FEAT-24. Grafana Cloud's free tier (then ~$0.50/GB) gives searchable logs and alerting without Datadog's per-host pricing. Operational telemetry never substitutes for the FEAT-13 trail, which lives in Postgres. |

| Grafana Cloud as the single stack (no Sentry) | Free tier; logs ~$0.50/GB ingested | Medium — OpenTelemetry setup, build own error views | High | Low — open-source components | OpenTelemetry | Cost pressure forces dropping Sentry's $26/month and the team is comfortable building error triage on logs and traces |
| Datadog | Infrastructure $15/host/month, APM $31/host/month, logs $0.10/GB | Medium | Very high | High — proprietary agent | Datadog | The product moves to container hosting with many hosts and a dedicated ops function wanting one proprietary suite |

### Indicative Cost Model

Order-of-magnitude only; verify current pricing before committing. "Launch" is the first months at hundreds to low thousands of freelancers; "Growth" is the year-one "few thousand freelancers" tier (Section 2).

| Component | Launch (order of magnitude) | Growth tier |
|-----------|-----------------------------|-------------|
| Vercel Pro (hosting, CDN, previews) | ~$20/month (1 seat, within $20 usage credit) | ~$40–100/month (2–3 seats plus usage beyond credit) |
| Neon Postgres (Launch → Scale plan) | ~$10–25/month ($0.106/CU-hour with scale-to-zero; few GB at $0.35/GB-month) | ~$50–160/month (Scale plan, ~1 CU sustained at $0.222/CU-hour) |
| Cloudflare R2 (deliverables, archives, logos) | ~$0–15/month (10 GB free; up to ~1 TB at $0.015/GB-month; zero egress) | ~$150–300/month at 10–20 TB stored (feasibility estimate; storage-allowance decision pending, Open Question 2) |
| Resend (transactional email) | Free (3,000/month) to ~$20/month (Pro, 50,000 emails) | ~$20–90/month, volume-scaled beyond 50,000 emails |
| Trigger.dev (jobs and schedules) | Free (50K runs/month) | ~$10–50/month usage-scaled |
| Sentry Team (errors, crons, uptime) | ~$26/month | ~$26–80/month with error overage |
| Grafana Cloud (logs) | Free tier | ~$5–25/month (~$0.50/GB ingested) |
| PostHog Cloud (analytics) | Free (1M events/month) | ~$0–50/month ($0.00005/event beyond free) |
| GitHub Actions (CI) | Free (2,000 min/month) | ~$4/user/month Team plan plus ~$0–20/month overage at $0.006/min |
| Documenso (e-signature, FEAT-26 v1 only) | ~$30/month (Individual) once FEAT-26 ships | ~$250/month (Platform) if white-label embedding is required, or ~$12/month self-hosted on a small container |
| Stripe Billing + card fees on the freelancer's own plan (revenue-proportional, not infrastructure) | ~$10–50/month (0.7% Billing plus 2.9% + 30c per charge on early subscriptions) | ~$500–1,500/month at ~1,000 paying freelancers on a $15/month plan |
| Stripe Connect on client invoice payments | $0 to the platform (direct charges bill the freelancer's own account) | $0 to the platform |

At launch the infrastructure lines (excluding Stripe's revenue-proportional fees) total roughly $80–130/month, close to the "under roughly $100/month" constraint; at the growth tier object storage alone can exceed the budget, which is the tension surfaced in feasibility Open Question 2 and must be resolved by the storage-allowance or budget decision rather than by the architecture.

### Local Development Setup

Prerequisites: Node.js LTS, pnpm, Docker (for local Postgres and optional MinIO), the Stripe CLI, and the Trigger.dev CLI. Setup path: clone → `pnpm install` → copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill test keys (Stripe test mode, Resend test key, Documenso free/test account, R2 dev bucket or MinIO endpoint, Trigger.dev dev key) → `docker compose up -d postgres minio` (or point `DATABASE_URL` at a personal Neon branch) → `pnpm db:migrate && pnpm db:seed` → in separate terminals `pnpm dev`, `pnpm trigger:dev`, and `stripe listen --forward-to localhost:3000/api/webhooks/stripe-connect`. Local substitutes: Docker Postgres for Neon, MinIO for R2 (S3 API), Stripe test mode and CLI webhooks, Resend test key (emails viewable in the Resend dashboard or React Email preview at `pnpm email:dev`), Trigger.dev local dev runner; Sentry and PostHog are disabled when their DSN/key is unset.

# Part G3 — Database Schema

The complete database schema: 45 entities, 49 tables and 101 relationships.


# Database Schema Design -- Clientroom

<!-- Reading guide (not part of the template rules): Table names are singular snake_case. FK columns are `{parent_table_singular}_id` unless a role prefix is needed (invited_by_user_id, accepted_by_contact_id, ...). All primary keys are `id uuid DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()`. All timestamps are `timestamptz`. `freelancer_account_id` is the tenant key (Section 4 multi-tenancy decision). Money is `numeric(20,0)` holding integer minor units of the row's ISO 4217 currency (ADR-016, ADR-028), so the column type is an exact DECIMAL and never INTEGER/FLOAT (Section 9, check 4). `user` is a reserved word in PostgreSQL and is always quoted ("user"), as Better Auth does by default. -->

## 1. Schema Overview

- **Database:** Neon serverless Postgres (Launch plan at launch; Scale plan when sustained load or retention needs grow; one project with branches for preview/staging) -- technical-architecture.md Section 3, ADR-003.
- **ORM:** Drizzle ORM v1 with drizzle-kit migrations, Neon serverless driver in WebSocket/Pool mode so interactive transactions (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) work from Vercel functions and Trigger.dev tasks -- Section 3, ADR-004.
- **Tables:** 49 (45 domain entities + 1 junction table + 3 lookup tables). The 45 entity tables are the 23 Stage 3 entities (21 from Shared Data Entities plus Accounting Export File and Data Export Archive, per technical-profile.md Section 5) and 22 implicit entities discovered from the specs and the architecture (Step 1 sweep, tagged in each table's Source line).
- **Relationships:** 101 (88 one-to-many, 1 many-to-many, 12 one-to-one). Each FK is one relationship; the many-to-many relationship is counted once although its junction table carries two FKs.
- **Migration strategy:** migration-based, consistent with technical-architecture.md Section 6 and ADR-020: every change is generated by `drizzle-kit generate` as a reviewed, committed SQL file and applied by `drizzle-kit migrate` in CI to preview branches, staging and production. Constructs Drizzle's schema DSL cannot express (row-level security policies, immutability triggers, partial and expression indexes, `tsvector` generated columns, cross-column CHECKs, the two-phase deletion helpers) are hand-authored as custom migration files in the same reviewed chain.

### Entity Map

**Domain Entities (Stage 3 -- 23):**
- freelancer_account -> belongs to user; has one branding_profile, subscription_plan, payment_account_connection, custom_domain, referral_attribution, storage_usage, invoice_counter; has many client, notification, support_access_session, data_export_archive, accounting_export_file, activity_log_entry, financial_totals (and is the tenant key on every owned table)
- client -> belongs to freelancer_account; has many client_contact, project
- client_contact -> belongs to client; actor on proposal acceptance, milestone approval, comment, payment; has many portal_token, portal_session
- project -> belongs to client; has many proposal, milestone, invoice; has one payment_schedule
- proposal -> belongs to project; has one proposal_signature; references payment_schedule; has many comment (change requests), proposal_resend_event
- payment_schedule -> belongs to project (one per project); has many payment_schedule_change
- milestone -> belongs to project; has many deliverable, comment; may trigger many invoice
- deliverable -> belongs to milestone; has many deliverable_version, upload_session
- deliverable_version -> belongs to deliverable; anchors many comment
- comment -> pinned to exactly one of deliverable_version, milestone, proposal; may reply to comment
- invoice -> belongs to project; has one invoice_snapshot; has many payment, reminder_log; addressed to many client_contact; may correct an invoice
- payment -> belongs to invoice
- reminder_log -> belongs to invoice; links the notification it sent
- activity_log_entry -> belongs to freelancer_account and usually project; has one activity_log_entry_subject
- notification -> belongs to freelancer_account; references notification_type, project and the recipient
- branding_profile, subscription_plan, payment_account_connection, custom_domain, referral_attribution -> each belongs to one freelancer_account
- support_access_session -> belongs to freelancer_account; opened by an operator user
- accounting_export_file, data_export_archive -> belong to freelancer_account

**Domain Entities (Implicit -- 22):** user, auth_account, auth_session, auth_verification, email_change_request, auth_rate_limit (identity/session, Section 11); portal_token, portal_session (portal realm, Section 11); proposal_signature (FEAT-26), proposal_resend_event (FEAT-02.SPEC-007), payment_schedule_change (FEAT-04 change_history), invoice_snapshot (FEAT-09.SPEC-007), activity_log_entry_subject (FEAT-13.SPEC-004), notification_preference (FEAT-21.SPEC-008), help_tip_dismissal (FEAT-30), feed_item_read_state (FEAT-29.SPEC-003), storage_usage (FEAT-16.SPEC-005), financial_totals (FEAT-12.SPEC-004, ADR-013), upload_session (FEAT-16.SPEC-002, ADR-008), invoice_counter (FEAT-09.SPEC-007, ADR-014), inbound_event (ADR-023), job_outbox (ADR-012).

**Junction Tables:**
- client_contact_invoice -> connects client_contact <-> invoice (Invoice "addressed to the client's Primary contact(s)", feature-dependency-map.md Invoice relationships)

**Lookup Tables:**
- invoice_status -> referenced by invoice (10 values, more than 8)
- notification_type -> referenced by notification, notification_preference (29 registered types)
- activity_event_type -> referenced by activity_log_entry (closed vocabulary plus extensions, more than 8 values)

## 2. Table Definitions

Conventions that apply to every table below and are not repeated in Notes cells: `id` is `uuid` PK default `gen_random_uuid()`; `created_at` and `updated_at` are `timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()` (`updated_at` is refreshed on every write by the ORM `$onUpdate` hook or a trigger; on append-only tables it simply never changes after insert). Every `freelancer_account_id` column is the tenant key (Section 4). "FK idx" means an index on the FK column; where a UNIQUE or composite index already leads with the FK column it is the FK index. Nullable FK columns use partial indexes (`WHERE col IS NOT NULL`). Enum type names are defined in Section 8. Monetary columns end in `_minor` and hold integer minor units in `numeric(20,0)`.

### user

**Source:** Implicit (identity decision, technical-architecture.md Section 11 "Authentication & Identity" and "User Model Fields"; Better Auth `user` table)
**Lifecycle:** Created by FEAT-20 (sign-up) and by operator provisioning (Better Auth admin plugin). Read by every authenticated screen. Updated by FEAT-21 (profile name; sign-in email on confirmed change, FEAT-21.SPEC-005). Deleted by FEAT-24 (account deletion).

| Column | Type | Nullable | Default | Constraints | Notes |
|--------|------|----------|---------|-------------|-------|
| id | uuid | NO | gen_random_uuid() | PK | |
| email | varchar(255) | NO | -- | UNIQUE on lower(email); CHECK (email ~* '^[^@[:space:]]+@[^@[:space:]]+$') | Source field: "sign-in email" (Freelancer Account). Email = bounded text with format constraint |
| email_verified_at | timestamptz | YES | -- | | NULL until verified (Section 11 email verification) |
| display_name | varchar(255) | NO | -- | | Source field: "name" (Freelancer Account) |
| role | user_role | NO | 'freelancer' | | `freelancer` or `operator` (Section 11 mapping) |
| created_at | timestamptz | NO | now() | | |
| updated_at | timestamptz | NO | now() | | Updated on every write |

**Indexes:**
- `user_pkey` -- PRIMARY KEY (id)
- `user_email_key` -- UNIQUE (lower(email))

**Lifecycle:** Created by FEAT-20 (sign-up) and FEAT-21.SPEC-003 (login method). Read by sign-in. Updated by FEAT-21.SPEC-003. Deleted with its user by FEAT-24.

### freelancer_account

**Source:** Freelancer Account from feature-dependency-map.md
**Lifecycle:** Created by FEAT-20. Read by FEAT-09, FEAT-14, FEAT-23, FEAT-31, FEAT-33. Updated by FEAT-21 (profile, business details, payment terms, sign-in email, sessions), FEAT-15 (time zone), FEAT-20 (onboarding), FEAT-24 (deletion state). Deleted by FEAT-24.

| Column | Type | Nullable | Default | Constraints | Notes |
|--------|------|----------|---------|-------------|-------|
| id | uuid | NO | gen_random_uuid() | PK | Tenant key referenced by every owned table |
| user_id | uuid | NO | -- | FK -> "user"(id), UNIQUE | One-to-one with the freelancer's user (Section 11) |
| handle | varchar(63) | NO | -- | UNIQUE; CHECK (handle ~ '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,61}[a-z0-9]$') | Slug in `/portal/[handle]` (ADR-021). Slug = UNIQUE |
| business_name | varchar(255) | YES | -- | | Source field: "business_name" (required before first invoice is sent, so NULL until set) |
| business_address | text | YES | -- | | Source field: "business_address" (multi-line address = unbounded text) |
| tax_id | varchar(64) | YES | -- | | Source field: "tax_id" |
| default_payment_terms_days | integer | NO | 0 | CHECK (default_payment_terms_days BETWEEN 0 AND 365) | Source field: "default_payment_terms"; 0 = due on receipt, N = within N days |
| time_zone | varchar(64) | NO | 'UTC' | | IANA zone name (ADR-016); source field "time_zone" (FEAT-15) |
| onboarding_state | onboarding_state | NO | 'in_progress' | | FEAT-20.SPEC-003 onboarding-progress state |
| onboarding_completed_at | timestamptz | YES | -- | CHECK ((onboarding_state = 'complete') = (onboarding_completed_at IS NOT NULL)) | FEAT-20.SPEC-003 "record the completion timestamp" |
| how_did_you_hear_resolved | boolean | NO | false | | FEAT-20.SPEC-003/004 `onboarding_how_did_you_hear_resolved` flag |
| referral_token | varchar(32) | NO | -- | UNIQUE | Token in the public `/r/[referralToken]` link (Section 11 protected routes; FEAT-33) |
| deletion_state | deletion_state | NO | 'active' | | Account deletion progress (FEAT-24.SPEC-004; states per Section 11). Relocated from `user` because operators have no deletion lifecycle |
| deletion_requested_at | timestamptz | YES | -- | | |
| deletion_committed_at | timestamptz | YES | -- | CHECK ((deletion_state = 'committed') = (deletion_committed_at IS NOT NULL)) | Retention clock start for `financial-record-legal-retention-period` (FEAT-24.SPEC-005) |
| created_at | timestamptz | NO | now() | | |
| updated_at | timestamptz | NO | now() | | Updated on every write |

Notes: `notification_preferences`, signed-in devices and help-tip dismissals are not columns (1NF) -- see notification_preference, auth_session, help_tip_dismissal. Sign-in credentials never appear here.

**Indexes:**
- `freelancer_account_pkey` -- PRIMARY KEY (id)
- `freelancer_account_user_id_key` -- UNIQUE (user_id) -- FK index
- `freelancer_account_handle_key` -- UNIQUE (handle)
- `freelancer_account_referral_token_key` -- UNIQUE (referral_token)

### subscription_plan

**Source:** Subscription Plan from feature-dependency-map.md
**Lifecycle:** Created by FEAT-23 (free tier, automatically at sign-up, FEAT-23.SPEC-002). Read by FEAT-01 (client-count limit), FEAT-31. Updated by FEAT-23 (upgrade, downgrade, cancel, lapse) and billing-capability status reports. Deleted by FEAT-24.

| Column | Type | Nullable | Default | Constraints | Notes |
|--------|------|----------|---------|-------------|-------|
| id | uuid | NO | gen_random_uuid() | PK | |
| freelancer_account_id | uuid | NO | -- | FK -> freelancer_account(id), UNIQUE | One per account |
| tier | subscription_tier | NO | 'free' | | Source field: "tier" |
| status | subscription_status | NO | 'active' | | Source field: "status" |
| billing_cycle | billing_cycle | YES | -- | | Source field: "billing_cycle"; NULL whenever tier is free (FEAT-23.SPEC-007) |
| current_period_end | timestamptz | YES | -- | | Reported by the billing capability (FEAT-23.SPEC-003) |
| last_failure_reason | varchar(255) | YES | -- | | FEAT-23.SPEC-007 supporting attributes |
| first_failure_at | timestamptz | YES | -- | | Grace window start (`subscription-charge-grace-window-days`) |
| retry_attempts_used | integer | NO | 0 | CHECK (retry_attempts_used >= 0) | |
| downgrade_eligible | boolean | NO | false | | Written by FEAT-23.SPEC-005 |
| billing_customer_ref | varchar(255) | YES | -- | | Reference only; payment details are held by Stripe Billing (ASMP-24) |
| billing_subscription_ref | varchar(255) | YES | -- | | Reference only |
| version | integer | NO | 1 | CHECK (version >= 1) | Optimistic-locking token (Section 4) |
| created_at | timestamptz | NO | now() | | |
| updated_at | timestamptz | NO | now() | | Updated on every write |

Constraint `subscription_plan_valid_state` encodes the only five legal states (FEAT-23.SPEC-007): CHECK ((tier = 'free' AND billing_cycle IS NULL AND status IN ('active','lapsed')) OR (tier = 'paid' AND billing_cycle IS NOT NULL AND status IN ('active','charge_failed','cancelled_at_period_end'))). `active_client_count` is derived live from client and is not stored.

**Indexes:**
- `subscription_plan_pkey` -- PRIMARY KEY (id)
- `subscription_plan_freelancer_account_id_key` -- UNIQUE (freelancer_account_id) -- FK index

Updated by FEAT-32 (reconnect) and processor status reports (FEAT-32.SPEC-003). Deleted by FEAT-32.SPEC-004 (disconnect) and FEAT-24.

**Source:** Proposal from feature-dependency-map.md
**Lifecycle:** Created by FEAT-02. Read by FEAT-03, FEAT-04, FEAT-13, FEAT-28, FEAT-31. Updated by FEAT-02 (edit before acceptance, which voids and re-sends), FEAT-03 (accepted state), FEAT-26 (signature). Deleted by FEAT-02 (unsent drafts only) and FEAT-24.

| Column | Type | Nullable | Default | Constraints | Notes |
|--------|------|----------|---------|-------------|-------|
| id | uuid | NO | gen_random_uuid() | PK | |

| project_id | uuid | NO | -- | FK -> project(id) | |
| predecessor_proposal_id | uuid | YES | -- | FK -> proposal(id) | Void-and-resend chain (FEAT-02.SPEC-006 "predecessor reference to the voided version") |
| copied_from_proposal_id | uuid | YES | -- | FK -> proposal(id) | Source field: "copied_from" |
| scope_description | text | NO | -- | CHECK (char_length(btrim(scope_description)) > 0) | Source field: "scope_description" |
| price_minor | numeric(20,0) | NO | -- | CHECK (price_minor > 0) | Source field: "price" (positive amount, FEAT-02.SPEC-010), minor units |
| currency | char(3) | NO | -- | CHECK (currency ~ '^[A-Z]{3}$') | Source field: "currency" -- frozen snapshot of the project currency at draft time (Section 6) |
| payment_schedule_id | uuid | YES | -- | FK -> payment_schedule(id) | Source field: "payment_schedule_reference"; locked at send (FEAT-02.SPEC-006) |
| status | proposal_status | NO | 'draft' | | Source field: "status" |
| sent_at | timestamptz | YES | -- | CHECK (status = 'draft' OR sent_at IS NOT NULL) | Source field: "sent_at" |
| voided_at | timestamptz | YES | -- | CHECK ((status = 'voided') = (voided_at IS NOT NULL)) | Set when superseded by an edit-and-resend |
| accepted_at | timestamptz | YES | -- | CHECK ((status = 'accepted') = (accepted_at IS NOT NULL)) | Source field: "accepted_at"; written once |
| accepted_by_contact_id | uuid | YES | -- | FK -> client_contact(id) | Source field: "accepted_by"; audit column (Section 4) |
| accepted_by_name | varchar(255) | YES | -- | CHECK ((status = 'accepted') = (accepted_by_name IS NOT NULL)) | Evidence snapshot of the accepting contact's name; survives contact erasure (XBR-27, ASMP-20) |

Immutability: once `status = 'accepted'` a trigger rejects any UPDATE of scope_description, price_minor, currency, payment_schedule_id, accepted_at, accepted_by_contact_id, accepted_by_name (XBR-04, ASMP-25). Sent and voided rows accept only status/void transitions.

| total_minor | numeric(20,0) | NO | -- | CHECK (total_minor >= amount_minor) | Source field: "total"; amount plus tax computed once at creation and stored as evidence (FEAT-09.SPEC-007); tax_amount = total - amount is derived |
| issue_date | date | NO | CURRENT_DATE | | Source field: "issue_date" |
| due_date | date | NO | -- | | Source field: "due_date"; derived from default payment terms, adjustable before sending |
| status_id | uuid | NO | -- | FK -> invoice_status(id) | Source field: "status" (10 values, lookup table) |
| reminder_paused | boolean | NO | false | | Source field: "reminder_paused" (FEAT-11) |
| sent_at | timestamptz | YES | -- | | Moment the invoice was sent (never edited after) |
| version | integer | NO | 1 | CHECK (version >= 1) | Status changes are reject-with-refresh against the current status (Contention line) |
| retention_hold_at | timestamptz | YES | -- | | Set by FEAT-24.SPEC-004 step 4 for records held under `financial-record-legal-retention-period`; cleared if deletion reverts |
| created_at | timestamptz | NO | now() | | |
| updated_at | timestamptz | NO | now() | | Updated on every write |

Notes: freelancer business details, client billing details and the tax line are frozen on invoice_snapshot. A credit note's amount never exceeding the original's total is a cross-row rule enforced by trigger. After `sent_at` is set, a trigger rejects UPDATE of everything except status_id, reminder_paused, version and retention_hold_at (XBR-04). `pay_link availability` is derived from payment_account_connection.

**Indexes:**
- `invoice_pkey` -- PRIMARY KEY (id)
- `invoice_account_number_key` -- UNIQUE (freelancer_account_id, invoice_number) -- gapless per-freelancer numbering (FEAT-09.SPEC-007); also the freelancer_account_id FK index
- `invoice_project_id_idx` -- INDEX (project_id) WHERE project_id IS NOT NULL -- FK index (composite read index in Section 7)
- `invoice_corrected_invoice_id_idx` -- INDEX (corrected_invoice_id) WHERE corrected_invoice_id IS NOT NULL -- FK index
- `invoice_milestone_id_idx` -- INDEX (milestone_id) WHERE milestone_id IS NOT NULL -- FK index
- `invoice_status_id_idx` -- INDEX (status_id) -- FK index (composite read index in Section 7)

| overdue_total_minor | numeric(20,0) | NO | 0 | CHECK (overdue_total_minor >= 0) | Source field: "overdue_total" |

| updated_at | timestamptz | NO | now() | | Updated on every write |

- `financial_totals_client_id_idx` -- INDEX (client_id) WHERE client_id IS NOT NULL -- FK index

### portal_token

**Source:** Implicit ("Sign-in link/token (feature-internal, not a Domain Entity Inventory record)", FEAT-05.SPEC-006; Section 11 portal realm)
**Lifecycle:** Created by FEAT-05.SPEC-004 (issuance). Read and updated by FEAT-05.SPEC-005 (verification: Issued to Used) and FEAT-05.SPEC-004 (Issued to Invalidated on re-request; Issued to Expired by time). Never deleted while the contact exists (invalidation is a state transition); removed with the contact or account (FEAT-24).

| Column | Type | Nullable | Default | Constraints | Notes |
|--------|------|----------|---------|-------------|-------|
| id | uuid | NO | gen_random_uuid() | PK | |
| freelancer_account_id | uuid | NO | -- | FK -> freelancer_account(id) | Tenant key |
| client_contact_id | uuid | NO | -- | FK -> client_contact(id) | Source field: "client_contact" |
| token_hash | varchar(64) | NO | -- | UNIQUE | Source field: "token_value", stored only as a SHA-256 hash (Section 11) |
| status | portal_token_status | NO | 'issued' | | Source field: "status" |
| issued_at | timestamptz | NO | now() | | Source field: "issued_at" |
| expires_at | timestamptz | NO | -- | CHECK (expires_at > issued_at) | issued_at + `magic-link-expiry-window` (24 h); expiry boundary is exclusive (FEAT-05.SPEC-006) |
| used_at | timestamptz | YES | -- | CHECK ((status = 'used') = (used_at IS NOT NULL)) | Source field: "used_at" |
| created_at | timestamptz | NO | now() | | |
| updated_at | timestamptz | NO | now() | | Updated on every write |

**Indexes:**
- `portal_token_pkey` -- PRIMARY KEY (id)
- `portal_token_token_hash_key` -- UNIQUE (token_hash)
- `portal_token_contact_issued_key` -- UNIQUE (client_contact_id) WHERE status = 'issued' -- at most one Issued token per contact (FEAT-05.SPEC-006 cross-field rule); also the client_contact_id FK index
- `portal_token_freelancer_account_id_idx` -- INDEX (freelancer_account_id) -- FK index

Invoice, Payment and Activity Log Entry parents use SET NULL so those records can outlive account deletion under legal retention (FEAT-24.SPEC-004/005, FEAT-13.SPEC-006); each such child carries a CHECK tying the NULL parent to `retention_hold_at` (Section 2).

Cascade rationale (each traces to the Delete/Archive cells cited in Section 4): children that cannot exist without the parent CASCADE (milestone to deliverable per FEAT-04 cell, deliverable to version, comment targets, account-owned rows on FEAT-24 deletion); evidence and attribution references SET NULL so an erased or deleted actor never deletes evidence (XBR-27, FEAT-13.SPEC-006); `client -> project` is RESTRICT because projects are never deleted in-product (FEAT-01 Non-Goals) and `invoice -> payment`, `invoice -> invoice (corrects)` and lookup FKs are RESTRICT so retention purge must delete children first. Deletion jobs (FEAT-24.SPEC-004 steps 7-9, FEAT-24.SPEC-005 purge) delete in child-before-parent order.

## 4. Data Lifecycle & Integrity Decisions

**Multi-tenancy:** Multi-tenant, shared schema with the Freelancer Account as the tenant. Every account-owned table carries `freelancer_account_id` as the tenant key (NOT NULL, FK to freelancer_account, ON DELETE CASCADE except the retention-capable tables invoice, payment and activity_log_entry, which detach and carry `retention_hold_at`), and every Section 5 policy scopes by it. Evidence: BRIEF.md Privacy ("strict isolation between clients") and ASMP-23 ("a client never sees another client's anything"); feature-dependency-map.md Freelancer Account "Owns every Client, Project, Branding Profile, Subscription Plan, Payment Account Connection, Referral Attribution, and Activity Log Entry"; Sec 11 "every query scoped by `freelancer_account_id`". No organization or team level exists above the account, so the tenant column is `freelancer_account_id` itself rather than a separate `tenant_id`: solo freelancers only (SC-01, cited in FEAT-01 Non-Goals), and a separate `tenant_id` would duplicate the same value. Schema-per-tenant and database-per-tenant are rejected because a few thousand tenants (ASMP-22) would multiply migrations across Neon branches (ADR-020) for no isolation benefit that row-level security does not already give. Tables scoped only through a parent (invoice_snapshot, activity_log_entry_subject, client_contact_invoice, and the auth tables) are protected by policies joining to the tenant-keyed parent.

## 5. Security & Access Model

**Enforcement model:** Row-level security (RLS) -- Neon Postgres supports it, so RLS is the primary authorization mechanism at the data layer, with `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` on every table and the application guard (`defineAction` / `defineQuery`, Section 10) as the first, defense-in-depth layer computing the same predicates. Interactive transactions on the Neon Pool driver (Section 3, ADR-004) let each request run `SET LOCAL app.realm = ..., app.freelancer_account_id = ..., app.client_id = ..., app.client_contact_id = ..., app.portal_role = ..., app.support_freelancer_account_id = ...` before its queries, so the settings cannot leak across pooled connections. Roles are exactly the four Section 11 roles (Nadia = `freelancer`, Owen = portal `primary`, Priya = portal `reviewer`, Dana = `operator`); the database principals used to run them are `app_runtime` (no BYPASSRLS), `app_operator_ro` (SELECT-only grants, the read-only connection Section 10 already requires for operator reads) and `app_system` (webhook processors, Trigger.dev tasks and sweeps, realm `system`, scoped per task by `app.freelancer_account_id` except the named cross-account sweeps). These principals are infrastructure, not additional product roles.

### Access Policies

Predicate shorthand: `FA` = `freelancer_account_id = current_setting('app.freelancer_account_id')::uuid`; `OWN_CLIENT` = the row belongs to the contact's client (`client_id = current_setting('app.client_id')::uuid` or reached through project/milestone to that client); `PRIMARY` = `current_setting('app.portal_role') = 'primary'`; `SUPPORT` = `freelancer_account_id = current_setting('app.support_freelancer_account_id')::uuid` AND an open support_access_session exists. | portal_token, portal_session | (none) | Owen, Priya, Nadia, Dana | No role policy: issuance and verification run as `app_system` in the unauthenticated verification flow (FEAT-05.SPEC-004/005); Sec 11 gives Dana None on portal access |
| upload_session, inbound_event, job_outbox | (none beyond Nadia's upload_session above) | all product roles | No product-role access; `app_system` only |

### Sensitive Fields

| Table | Column(s) | Sensitivity (source) | Protection Note |
|-------|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| client | billing_name, billing_address, tax_id | GDPR-class personal data; may identify a sole trader (feature-dependency-map.md Client Data Sensitivity, ASMP-24) | Encrypt at rest (Neon storage encryption plus application-level column encryption for billing_address); mask in list and log surfaces (roster shows client_name only); excluded from the portal `client` view; erased/exported per FEAT-24 |
| client_contact | name, email | GDPR-class personal data (Client Contact Data Sensitivity, ASMP-24) | Erased in place on removal (XBR-27, FEAT-18.SPEC-009); email masked in logs and Sentry (ADR-031 PII scrubbing); restricted read set: Nadia and Dana in a support session; never visible to another client |
| proposal | scope_description, price_minor, accepted_by_name | Commercially confidential and evidentiary; accepter identity is personal data (Proposal Data Sensitivity, ASMP-15, ASMP-24) | Immutable once accepted (trigger); Reviewer read set excludes the table (Sec 11); accepted_by_name retained after contact erasure by design (XBR-27); masked from operator exports (none allowed) |
| proposal_signature | signer_legal_name, signer_email, signature_data | Signer identity GDPR-class, retained as evidence (architecture Section 8 Documenso row, XBR-27) | Encrypt signature_data at rest; read set Nadia, the signing Primary contact and Dana (view); excluded from logs |
| milestone | price_minor, approved_by_name | Business-confidential pricing; approver identity personal data (Milestone Data Sensitivity, ASMP-24) | approved_by_name retained after erasure; price columns follow the milestone read set in Section 5 policies |
| payment_schedule | deposit_amount_minor, completion_amount_minor | Business-confidential pricing terms, no personal data (Payment Schedule Data Sensitivity) | Freelancer and Dana only; no client policy |
| comment | body, author identity | Personal data and free text that may mention individuals, GDPR-class (Comment Data Sensitivity, ASMP-24) | Isolated per client by policy; included in export and removed on account deletion (FEAT-24); body excluded from logs and analytics events (ADR-015, ADR-031) |
| deliverable, deliverable_version | display_name, storage_object_key, file content | Client-confidential work product that may contain personal data; operator lists but never downloads (Deliverable Data Sensitivity, ASMP-18, XBR-29) | Private bucket with short-lived presigned GETs per authorized viewer; `storage_object_key` column privilege revoked from `app_operator_ro`; `/api/files` refuses operators (Sec 11) |
| invoice, invoice_snapshot | client_billing_name, client_billing_address, client_tax_id, freelancer_business_*, amounts | Financial record with personal data, GDPR-class, evidentiary and immutable once sent, legal retention (Invoice Data Sensitivity, ASMP-24, ASMP-25, SC-24) | Encrypt billing and business address columns at rest; Reviewer read set excludes invoices; snapshot isolated in its own table so list queries never touch PII; retained rows inaccessible after account deletion (tenant NULL) and purged after `financial-record-legal-retention-period` |
| payment | processor_payment_ref, initiated_by_contact_id, recorded_by_user_id, refund_reason | Financial record, payer identity personal data, no card or bank credentials ever stored (Payment Data Sensitivity, ASMP-24, SC-10) | References only; refund_reason masked in list and log surfaces; same retention as invoice |
| activity_log_entry | actor_name, detail | Actor identities are GDPR-class personal data and entries are immutable evidence (Activity Log Entry Data Sensitivity, ASMP-25) | Read set Nadia and Dana; `detail` must not hold email addresses or message bodies (writer rule); logs and traces exclude the table content; financial-character entries follow the 7-year hold (FEAT-13.SPEC-006) |
| freelancer_account | business_name, business_address, tax_id | Personal data of the freelancer, GDPR-class (Freelancer Account Data Sensitivity, ASMP-24) | Encrypt business_address and tax_id at rest; exportable and deletable (ASMP-23); Dana reads in a support session |
| user, auth_account | email, password_hash | Personal data; sign-in credentials never visible to the operator (Freelancer Account Data Sensitivity) | password_hash never selectable by any product role, only the Better Auth adapter under `app_system`; email masked in logs; unique on lower(email) |
| auth_session, portal_session, portal_token, auth_verification, email_change_request | token_hash, value_hash, user_agent, ip_address | Credentials and network identifiers (Sec 11: tokens stored only as SHA-256 hashes) | Hashes only, raw tokens live solely in emailed links and cookies; ip_address and user_agent masked in logs; no product-role read except the owner's own session list |
| notification | recipient_email | Personal data, GDPR-class (Notification Data Sensitivity, ASMP-24) | Nulled when the contact is erased; not selectable by Dana; masked in logs (ADR-031) |
| support_access_session | request_text, operator_user_id | Freelancer's support request text and operator identity, personal data (Support Access Session Data Sensitivity) | Nadia and the operator only; every open and close writes a trail entry and an email (XBR-29) |
| referral_attribution | referring_freelancer_account_id, self_reported_source | Low personal data, aggregate use only (Referral Attribution Data Sensitivity) | No role read policy; the referrer is never told who signed up (FEAT-33); queried in aggregate by `app_system` |
| payment_account_connection | processor_account_ref | Financial-account linkage, reference only (Payment Account Connection Data Sensitivity, SC-10) | Hidden from the operator; masked in logs |
| subscription_plan | billing_customer_ref, billing_subscription_ref | Billing relationship references; payment details held by Stripe (Subscription Plan Data Sensitivity, ASMP-24) | References only; excluded from the Dana column set |
| inbound_event | payload | Provider webhook bodies may contain recipient emails and payer references (architecture Section 8) | `app_system` only; 90-day retention after processing; excluded from logs |
| data_export_archive | storage_object_key | Archive of the freelancer's entire personal-data set (FEAT-24, ASMP-23) | Private bucket, presigned single-use link for Nadia only; purged after 7 days |

No field is marked "special-category" by any spec (feature-dependency-map.md Project Data Sensitivity: "no special-category data"); the classifications above are the GDPR-class markings the specs apply.

## 6. Normalization Log

### Changes Applied

| Entity | Field | Violation | Resolution |
|--------|-------|-----------|------------|
| Client | currency and tax treatment | 3NF: depends on the project, not the client (FEAT-15.SPEC-001 configures it per project) | Stored only on project (`currency`, `tax_label`, `tax_rate`); not duplicated on client |
| Project | stage | 3NF: derived from proposal, milestone, invoice, completion and cancellation state (FEAT-01.SPEC-011) | Not stored; derived at read time |
| Project | lock_state | 3NF: derived from whether an invoice has been sent (FEAT-15.SPEC-004) | Not stored |
| Freelancer Account | notification_preferences (set of per-type toggles) | 1NF: repeating group | New table notification_preference (one row per account and type) |
| Freelancer Account | signed-in devices | 1NF: repeating group | Modelled by auth_session (one row per session) |
| Freelancer Account, Client Contact | help-tip dismissals | 1NF: repeating group | New table help_tip_dismissal; Section 11's `help_dismissals` column on the contact is not created |
| Freelancer Account | pending sign-in email change (target email, token, expiry) | 3NF: independent attributes with their own lifecycle | New table email_change_request; Section 11's `pending_email` and `pending_email_expires_at` columns on user are not created |
| Freelancer Account | time_zone, onboarding_state, deletion_state, deleted_at (listed on `user` in Section 11) | 2NF/3NF: apply only to freelancers, not operators | Placed on freelancer_account (one-to-one with user); `deleted_at` replaced by the two-phase `deletion_state` with committed timestamp because the account row is hard-deleted (FEAT-24.SPEC-004) |
| Freelancer Account | name and sign-in email | 3NF: already owned by the user identity | Stored once on user (`display_name`, `email`) |
| Payment Schedule | change_history | 1NF: repeating group | New table payment_schedule_change |
| Proposal | signature record (signer identity, signature data, timestamp) | 1NF/2NF: optional evidence block that exists only for opted-in proposals (v1) and holds personal data | Split to one-to-one proposal_signature |
| Proposal | currency | 3NF: equals the project's currency | Kept deliberately as an immutable evidence snapshot: an accepted proposal's content is immutable while the project's currency stays editable until the first invoice is sent (FEAT-15.SPEC-004, XBR-04) |
| Deliverable | size | 3NF: depends on the file version | Stored as deliverable_version.size_bytes only |
| Deliverable Version | is_latest | 3NF: derived (highest round_number) | Not stored (FEAT-17.SPEC-003) |
| Invoice | freelancer business details, client billing details, tax label and rate | 3NF/PII: values copied from other entities at creation and required to survive project and account deletion during legal retention | Moved to one-to-one invoice_snapshot so the frozen evidence and the personal data are isolated from the hot invoice row |
| Invoice | tax amount | 3NF: total - amount | Not stored; total kept as immutable creation-time evidence (FEAT-09.SPEC-007) |
| Invoice | addressed-to contacts (plural) | 1NF: repeating group | Junction client_contact_invoice |
| Invoice | pay_link availability | 3NF: derived from payment_account_connection | Not stored |
| Invoice | status (10 values) | Enum threshold: more than 8 values | Lookup table invoice_status |
| Payment | currency | 3NF: equals the invoice's currency | Not stored on payment |
| Payment | refunded amount and reason | Not a repeating group: at most one refund per invoice (FEAT-25.SPEC-003 stale-state rejection) | Kept as nullable columns on payment |
| Comment | target (deliverable version, milestone or proposal) | Polymorphic association (anti-pattern 8) | Three nullable FKs with a CHECK requiring exactly one |
| Activity Log Entry | affected_record | Polymorphic association (anti-pattern 8) and a 20+ column table if inlined | Exclusive nullable FKs moved to one-to-one activity_log_entry_subject with CHECK at most one and a kind/label snapshot |
| Activity Log Entry | actor (freelancer, contact, operator or system) | Two identity realms cannot share one FK | actor_kind plus two nullable FKs with a CHECK |
| Notification | triggering event reference | Polymorphic association (anti-pattern 8) | Idempotency `dedupe_key` (opaque, not a foreign reference) plus the real `project_id` FK |
| Notification | notification_type (29 values with classification) | Enum threshold: more than 8 values with metadata | Lookup table notification_type |
| Activity Log Entry | event_type (24+ values) | Enum threshold | Lookup table activity_event_type |
| Feed item | read state (source: Notification or Activity Log Entry) | Polymorphic association (anti-pattern 8) | Exclusive nullable FKs with CHECK exactly one |
| Tenant key | freelancer_account_id on every owned table | 3NF: transitively determined through project/client/account | Deliberate, not performance denormalization: the Step 5.5 tenancy decision requires the tenant column on every tenant-owned table so RLS predicates stay single-table; the implementing team should add composite FKs `(parent_id, freelancer_account_id)` to parent `UNIQUE (id, freelancer_account_id)` on the hot parent-child pairs so the column can never disagree with the parent chain |

### Denormalization Candidates (for the implementing team)

| Pattern | Tables Involved | Rationale for Deferral |
|---------|----------------|----------------------|
| Roster shows each project's derived stage (FEAT-01.SPEC-011) | project, proposal, milestone, invoice | Stage derivation reads 4 tables; normalize first, measure the roster, then consider a stored stage refreshed on state change |
| Portal home lists a contact's projects with next action and unpaid invoices (FEAT-05.SPEC-003) | client_contact, project, milestone, invoice | 4-table join; the largest mobile-latency risk (ASMP-21); measure before adding a read model |
| Invoice detail with reminder history, payments and party details (FEAT-09.SPEC-002) | invoice, invoice_snapshot, payment, reminder_log | 4-table join for one screen; acceptable at single-invoice scope |
| Activity trail with subject labels and actor names (FEAT-13.SPEC-001) | activity_log_entry, activity_log_entry_subject, activity_event_type | 3-table join per row on the longest list; consider a joined view before any copy |
| Dashboard totals (FEAT-12) | invoice, payment, project, client | Already handled by the `financial_totals` read model chosen in ADR-013; no further denormalization proposed |
| Active client count for the limit check (FEAT-01.SPEC-008) | client, subscription_plan | Count computed live from the partial index in Section 7; a counter column would be a decision for after measurement |

Baseline (PK, FK, unique) indexes are defined per table in Section 2 and are not repeated here.

| client_active_by_account_idx | client | (freelancer_account_id) WHERE status = 'active' | btree partial | Active-client count at every add or reactivate (FEAT-01.SPEC-008) and the roster's default Active filter (FEAT-01.SPEC-003) |

| activity_retention_hold_idx | activity_log_entry | (retention_hold_at) WHERE retention_hold_at IS NOT NULL | btree partial | Retained-entry purge (FEAT-13.SPEC-006) |

| client_contact_active_role_idx | client_contact | (client_id, role) WHERE status = 'active' | btree partial | Primary-contact existence check at commit (FEAT-18.SPEC-006, XBR-07) and Primary-recipient resolution for emails (FEAT-14.SPEC-002) |
| notification_delivery_warning_idx | notification | (project_id) WHERE delivery_status IN ('failed','bounced') AND warning_raised_at IS NOT NULL | btree partial | Delivery-failure warning on a project (FEAT-14.SPEC-006); Contact List hub lists warnings (technical-profile.md Section 2, FEAT-18) |
| notification_retry_idx | notification | (delivery_status, updated_at) WHERE delivery_status IN ('queued','failed') | btree partial | Retry sweep for transient failures within the retry window (FEAT-14.SPEC-003) |
| job_outbox_pending_idx | job_outbox | (run_after) WHERE acknowledged_at IS NULL | btree partial | One-minute Trigger.dev sweep re-dispatches unacknowledged rows (ADR-012) |

| support_access_session_open_idx | support_access_session | (last_activity_at) WHERE opened_at IS NOT NULL AND closed_at IS NULL | btree partial | 15-minute inactivity auto-close sweep (FEAT-31.SPEC-004, Sec 11) |
| support_access_session_pending_idx | support_access_session | (created_at) WHERE opened_at IS NULL | btree partial | Operator console lists pending requests (FEAT-31.SPEC-002) |
| data_export_archive_expiry_idx | data_export_archive | (expires_at) WHERE file_purged_at IS NULL AND expires_at IS NOT NULL | btree partial | Archive file purge after the 7-day window (FEAT-24.SPEC-003) |
| upload_session_expiry_idx | upload_session | (expires_at) WHERE status IN ('open','completing') | btree partial | Expiry and abort sweep of stale multipart sessions (FEAT-16.SPEC-002, ADR-008) |
| portal_session_expiry_idx | portal_session | (expires_at) | btree | Expired-session sweep (Sec 11 30-day rolling lifetime) |
| auth_session_expiry_idx | auth_session | (expires_at) | btree | Expired-session sweep (Sec 11) |
| client_search_idx | client | to_tsvector('simple', client_name) using GIN, plus client_name gin_trgm_ops | GIN full-text and trigram | Global Search over clients (FEAT-28.SPEC-001/002, technical-profile.md Search signal, ADR-011) |
| project_search_idx | project | to_tsvector('simple', project_name) using GIN, plus project_name gin_trgm_ops | GIN full-text and trigram | Global Search over projects (FEAT-28.SPEC-002, ADR-011) |
| proposal_search_idx | proposal | to_tsvector('simple', scope_description) using GIN | GIN full-text | Global Search over proposals (FEAT-28.SPEC-002, ADR-011); results scoped by tenant predicate (FEAT-28.SPEC-003) |
| deliverable_search_idx | deliverable | display_name gin_trgm_ops | GIN trigram | Global Search over deliverables (FEAT-01 Cross-Feature Touchpoints: search result opens a deliverable; ADR-011) |
| invoice_number_search_idx | invoice | (invoice_number::text) gin_trgm_ops | GIN trigram | Global Search matches invoice numbers by prefix (ADR-011 "pg_trgm ... names and invoice numbers", FEAT-28.SPEC-002) |

### Growth-Tier Notes

- **Partition `activity_log_entry` (and `inbound_event`) by month on `occurred_at` / `received_at`:** trigger when either exceeds tens of millions of rows or trail queries drift past the ~2 s interactivity target (ASMP-21); requires the immutability trigger and retention-hold purge to be partition-aware.
- **Read replica (Neon read replica) for the operator read-only connection and dashboard reads:** trigger when support-session reads or FEAT-12 aggregation contend with write latency on invoice payment flows.
- **Materialized read model for portal home or roster stage (Section 6 candidates):** trigger when the measured p95 of those joins exceeds the mobile target of roughly 2 seconds (ASMP-21).
- **Object-storage tiering or archival for old deliverable versions:** trigger when stored bytes threaten the roughly $100/month budget (architecture Section 2: ~20 TB could cost ~$300/month); the schema already tracks bytes in `storage_usage` and `deliverable_version.size_bytes`.
- **Increase Neon compute or move to the Scale plan:** trigger when sustained load or point-in-time-restore retention needs exceed the Launch plan (Section 3 database recommendation).
